Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. A couple of clarifying items from our side so we can get legal and security aligned:

1) Backups: we need to be explicit that automated snapshots for EU workloads are stored only in eu-west-1 unless we opt-in to cross-region replication. If cross-region replication is available, we need controls to opt-in and specify target regions.

2) Failover: in a large-scale outage in the EU region, would Redwood automatically fail traffic to a US region instance? Our preference is a controlled failover (manual or policy-driven) rather than automatic cross-border failover for compliance reasons.

3) Encryption & KMS: can we supply our own KMS keys (customer-managed keys) for encryption-at-rest of both primary storage and backups? If not, what are the guarantees around key locality and access?

4) Logs & PII: we need to know the default retention for request logs and whether Redwood can support a short TTL (e.g., 30 days) and automated scrubbing of PII fields prior to long-term storage.

If you can confirm these points (high level) we'll pass to our InfoSec and schedule the deep-dive.

Great questions, Oliver — summary answers below (high level). Aditya will follow with the detailed technical note and configuration examples.

Backups: By default, automated snapshots and scheduled backups for a tenant are stored in the same region where the compute and primary storage run. Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature we can enable for DR; when enabled you pick the target region(s). We will include the configuration snippet in Aditya's note.

Failover: Redwood supports two models:
- Policy-driven failover (recommended for regulated customers) — we keep primary tenancy pinned to the requested region; on outage, failover is initiated only when you or a configured policy triggers it (manual or automated policy with approval controls).
- Opportunistic automatic failover — routes to the nearest compatible pool if primary is unavailable (we do not enable cross-region auto-failover by default for customers who require data locality).

KMS / Encryption: Yes — we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS for both primary storage and backups. Keys remain under your AWS account; Redwood can be configured to use them so we never hold plaintext keys.

Logs & PII: Request logs are stored in-region by default. You can configure retention TTLs (30/90/365 days). We also support request masking (redact PII at the proxy layer) and a configurable pipeline to scrub or hash fields before long-term archival. We'll include an example retention policy and masking config.

Attachments: I've attached the region-pinning explainer and our SOC2 quick-reference for your security team.

Next step: Aditya — can you send the detailed technical doc with the exact configuration snippets (KMS ARN example, failover policy JSON, backup replication flags) and propose 2 slots for a 45-minute technical call next week?

Subject: RE: Region pinning and data residency - follow up & next steps (technical details)

Hi Oliver / Priya — following up with the technical details and config examples we discussed. I'll keep this tightly focused on region pinning, backups/replication, failover behavior, and logs/PII.

1) Region pinning (options)
- Tenant-level pinning: set the tenant's preferred region (e.g., "eu-west-1"). All inference, caches, and request logs are served and retained in-region.
- Route-level pinning: pin specific API keys/routes to regions if you have a mixed traffic model (e.g., EU traffic -> eu cluster, US traffic -> us cluster).
- Model variants: you can pin model variants per-region (helps with latency and compliance).

Example: tenant config snippet (high level)
{ "tenant_id": "acme-tenant-123", "region_pin": "eu-west-1", "route_pinning": {"/v1/generate-eu": "eu-west-1"} }

2) Backups and snapshots
- Default: snapshots/backups are written to the same region as the tenant's compute/storage.
- Cross-region replication: optional. If enabled, backups are replicated to specified region(s). Replication is asynchronous and can be configured per-namespace.
- Backup locality guarantees: when replication is disabled, data (including backups) never leaves the pinned region.

KMS: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS. Provide your KMS key ARN and we'll use it for EBS/volume encryption and backup encryption. Keys live in your AWS account and region.

3) Failover behavior
- Controlled failover (recommended): configure a policy (manual or policy-based with approvals) — Redwood will standby secondary capacity in another region but will only switch traffic after the configured approval window.
- Automatic failover: can be enabled for low-latency availability but will route to the nearest available region (cross-border). We do not enable this by default for regulated customers.

4) Logs, retention, and PII scrubbing
- Request logs stay in-region by default and can be streamed to customer-managed sinks (S3/GCS) in the same region.
- Retention TTL configurable per-tenant: 30/90/365 days.
- PII scrubbing: we support a masking pipeline (regex/field-level) that runs before long-term storage. For stronger isolation, you can enable request-side tokenization so PII never reaches Redwood's logs.

5) Backups for cross-region DR testing
- You can request on-demand cross-region restore tests. These are performed on ephemeral resources in the target region; they do not change production backup policies unless you opt-in.

6) Example commands & links
- Tenant pinning API (POST): https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/pin-region
- Backup replication flag: "replication": "disabled|eu-west-1->us-east-1"
